#!/usr/bin/bash
# ldap-authorized-keys -- sshd's own AuthorizedKeysCommand script.
# Invoked as: /usr/bin/bash /usr/sbin/ldap-authorized-keys %u
# Queries live LDAP (via the svc-nslcd service-account bind, never the
# connecting user's own credentials) for %u's sshPublicKey attribute
# and prints each key on its own line for sshd to accept.
USERNAME="$1"
. /etc/ldap-authkeys.conf

while IFS= read -r line; do
	case "$line" in
	sshPublicKey:\ *)
		echo "${line#sshPublicKey: }"
		;;
	esac
done < <(/usr/bin/ldapsearch -x -LLL -o ldif-wrap=no -H "$LDAP_URI" -D "$BIND_DN" -w "$BIND_PW" \
	-b "$LDAP_BASE" "(cn=$USERNAME)" sshPublicKey 2>/dev/null)

Port 22
HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key
HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key
PidFile /run/sshd.pid

UsePAM yes
PasswordAuthentication yes
PubkeyAuthentication yes
PermitRootLogin no

AuthorizedKeysCommand /usr/bin/bash /usr/sbin/ldap-authorized-keys %u
AuthorizedKeysCommandUser authkeys

# /etc/profile -- system-wide shell setup for every login on this box.
#
# Staged from the container recipe, deliberately: this is setup that
# should be here for every account, including one created after the
# fact -- so it belongs in the recipe, which is re-staged on every
# create, rather than in any one user's home. Per-user files live in
# ~, which is a persistent volume on this box (ADR-0183).

umask 022
export PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export LANG=C.UTF-8
export EDITOR=vim
export PAGER=less

# A real prompt. Red user@host when root, cyan otherwise, then the cwd --
# the point being that you can always see who and where you are on a box
# whose whole purpose is reaching other machines.
if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
	PS1='\[\033[1;31m\]\u@\h\[\033[0m\]:\[\033[1;34m\]\w\[\033[0m\]# '
else
	PS1='\[\033[1;36m\]\u@\h\[\033[0m\]:\[\033[1;34m\]\w\[\033[0m\]$ '
fi
export PS1

alias ll='ls -alF'
alias la='ls -A'
alias l='ls -CF'

# History worth having on a jump host: generous, de-duplicated, appended
# rather than overwritten so concurrent sessions don't clobber each other.
export HISTSIZE=10000
export HISTFILESIZE=20000
export HISTCONTROL=ignoredups:erasedups
shopt -s histappend 2>/dev/null || true
shopt -s checkwinsize 2>/dev/null || true

# Per-user customisation lives in ~/.bashrc, on the jump-home volume --
# it survives both a restart and a full recreate (ADR-0183).
if [ -r "$HOME/.bashrc" ]; then
	. "$HOME/.bashrc"
fi

# ~/.bashrc -- your own customisations.
#
# This home directory lives on the `jump-home` volume (ADR-0183), so
# anything you put here survives the container being restarted, and
# survives it being recreated -- which happens on its own whenever the
# jumpbox image is rebuilt (follow_rolling). Before volumes existed,
# every recreate silently took this file with it.
#
# Shell setup that should be there for EVERYONE still belongs in the
# container recipe's /etc/profile instead, so a brand-new account gets
# it too.

# Examples:
# alias k='kubectl'
# export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"
